skill.name: text-to-lottie
skill.description: Create, edit, and debug Lottie JSON for the local Skia Skottie player. Turn briefs or SVG artwork into logos, loaders, animated text, diagrams, and product scenes.
skill.summary: Turn text briefs and SVG artwork into editable Lottie scenes for Skottie.
skill.author: diffusionstudio

security_audit.summary: The 98 static alerts do not establish a security issue: they cover animation guidance, Markdown formatting, local previews, or a read-only JSON check. The separate player setup workflow can download and execute unpinned tooling and project code. No evidence found of exfiltration or instructions that attempt to manipulate the audit.

remediation.issue: Player setup can execute unreviewed code from mutable sources.
remediation.suggestion: Ask for approval before downloading or running setup code. Pin the bootstrap tool and player revision, use the reviewed lockfile, and review scripts before running them in an isolated workspace.

content.user_title: Create Lottie animations from text and SVG
content.value_statement: Turning a motion brief into Lottie requires careful timing and renderer checks. This skill creates or edits scenes and checks exact frames in the local Skottie player.
actual_capabilities: Turn written briefs into Lottie scenes for logos, loaders, titles, and interface feedback.
Animate supplied SVG artwork with path draws or grouped reveals while preserving its viewBox.
Stage chart reveals, count-up labels, diagram traces, and multi-part product sequences.
Expose supported colors, numbers, and native text as editable controls in the player.
Edit an existing scene and inspect specific frames for blank layers, missing assets, clipping, or timing problems.
limitations: Render verification requires the local Skottie player project and a running development server.
Native text needs a matching font file in the scene folder. Long edits can still overflow the text box.
Complex SVG filters, styles, and intersections may need to be rebuilt or simplified.
Skottie verification does not establish that the scene will render the same way in other Lottie players.

use_cases.title: Design Interface Feedback
use_cases.description: Create a transparent loader or success indicator and check its timing at icon size.

use_cases.title: Build Editable Brand Motion
use_cases.description: Animate an approved SVG logo or create a lower third with editable brand color and text.

use_cases.title: Debug an Existing Scene
use_cases.description: Find why a layer is blank or cropped and verify the fix in the requested scene.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Loader
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Create a new interface asset.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a transparent 48 by 48 Lottie spinner that loops once per second. Preview it at icon size in the local player.

prompt_templates.title: Animate a Logo
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the attached SVG to create a two-second logo reveal. Preserve the original proportions and colors. Keep the background transparent and compare the settled frame against the SVG.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Blank Title Text
prompt_templates.prompt: Fix the blank title in the specified Lottie scene. Use the supplied font, keep the title editable, and check frames where the title should be visible.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Product Sequence
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Coordinate multiple scenes and editable controls.
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn the supplied brief into three scenes: introduce the feature, show how it works, and close with the result. Use editable headline and accent color controls. Verify the opening, midpoint, and final frame of each scene.

output_examples.input: Create a small loading spinner with a transparent background.
output_examples.output: A transparent Lottie scene with a rotating arc and a continuous loop.

output_examples.input: Animate this SVG wordmark without distorting its letterforms.
output_examples.output: A logo reveal that holds the original wordmark at the end. The final frame preserves the proportions, fills, and holes of the SVG.

output_examples.input: Make a lower third with editable speaker name and role.
output_examples.output: A transparent overlay that enters, holds long enough to read, and exits. The player exposes separate controls for the speaker name and role.

best_practices: Specify the canvas size, duration, and background when they matter to the output.
Provide the source SVG and any font files needed for native text.
Review the opening, midpoint, and final visible frame in Skottie, then play the full scene to check timing.
anti_patterns: Do not assume that an animation that works in one Lottie player will look identical in another.
Do not replace an existing scene based solely on what the player currently shows.
Do not use a background rectangle for an asset that must remain transparent.

faq.question: What files does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It creates or updates a Lottie JSON scene. It can add a controls file when the scene needs editor labels or numeric ranges.

faq.question: Can it edit an existing animation?
faq.answer: Yes. Give the scene path or player route and describe what to change and what to keep.

faq.question: Can I start from an SVG?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill can animate SVG paths or groups. Complex filters or styles may need to be simplified for Skottie.

faq.question: Can I edit text after the animation is made?
faq.answer: Yes, when the scene exposes native text as a control. The scene folder must contain a font with the declared family name.

faq.question: Does the skill need internet access?
faq.answer: Preview checks use the local player. If the player is missing, the documented setup downloads project code and dependencies.

faq.question: How does the skill check the animation?
faq.answer: It checks that the scene JSON parses and inspects selected frames in Skottie. It does not certify compatibility with other renderers.
